subtopics.name: Reflection
definitions: Reflection: Change in direction of light when it bounces off a surface, with angle of incidence equal to angle of reflection

subtopics.name: Refraction
definitions: Refraction: Bending of light as it passes from one medium to another due to change in speed
Index of Refraction: Ratio of speed of light in vacuum to speed in medium
Total Internal Reflection: Complete reflection occurring when light travels from higher to lower index medium at angle greater than critical angle

subtopics.name: Lenses and Mirrors
definitions: Converging Lens: Lens that brings parallel rays to a focus (positive focal length)
Diverging Lens: Lens that spreads parallel rays (negative focal length)
Focal Length: Distance from lens/mirror to focal point where parallel rays converge

subtopics.name: Optical Instruments
definitions: Microscope: Optical instrument for viewing small objects with compound magnification
Telescope: Optical instrument for viewing distant objects using objective and eyepiece lenses

subtopics.name: Interference
formulas: d sin(θ) = mλ (Double Slit Constructive Interference)
2nt = mλ (Thin Film Constructive Interference at normal incidence)
I = I₁ + I₂ + 2√(I₁I₂)cos(δ) (Intensity with Phase Difference)
definitions: Interference: Superposition of waves resulting in amplitude changes
Constructive Interference: Waves adding to produce larger amplitude
Destructive Interference: Waves canceling to reduce amplitude

subtopics.name: Diffraction
definitions: Diffraction: Bending of waves around obstacles or through apertures
Diffraction Grating: Multiple slit device that separates light into spectrum
Resolution: Ability to distinguish between closely spaced objects

subtopics.name: Polarization
definitions: Polarization: Restriction of vibration of transverse waves to one direction
Linear Polarization: EM wave vibrations confined to single plane
Polarizer: Device that transmits waves of specific polarization while blocking others

subtopics.name: Photoelectric Effect
definitions: Photoelectric Effect: Emission of electrons from material when light of sufficient frequency strikes it
Work Function: Minimum energy needed to eject electron from material
Threshold Frequency: Minimum frequency of light that can cause photoelectric emission

subtopics.name: Wave-Particle Duality
definitions: Wave-Particle Duality: Principle that all particles exhibit both wave and particle properties
Photon: Quantum of electromagnetic energy with zero rest mass
de Broglie Wavelength: Wavelength associated with a particle of momentum p

subtopics.name: Quantum Electrodynamics
definitions: Quantum Electrodynamics: Quantum field theory of electromagnetic interactions
Virtual Photons: Transient quantum particles mediating electromagnetic force

subtopics.name: Electric Charge
definitions: Electric Charge: Fundamental property of matter that causes it to experience force in electromagnetic field
Conservation of Charge: Net charge in isolated system remains constant
Quantization of Charge: Charge exists as integer multiples of elementary charge e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C

subtopics.name: Electric Field
formulas: E = k|q|/r² (Electric Field of Point Charge)
definitions: Electric Field: Region around charged object where electric force acts on other charges
Field Lines: Visual representation of electric field direction and magnitude
Flux: Measure of electric field passing through surface

subtopics.name: Electric Potential
definitions: Electric Potential: Electric potential energy per unit charge
Voltage: Potential difference between two points
Equipotential Surface: Surface where electric potential is constant

subtopics.name: Capacitance
definitions: Capacitance: Ability of system to store electric charge
Capacitor: Device storing energy in electric field between conductors
Dielectric: Insulating material that increases capacitance

subtopics.name: Dielectrics
definitions: Dielectric: Non-conducting material that can be polarized by electric field
Dielectric Constant: Ratio of permittivity of material to permittivity of vacuum
Polarization: Alignment of electric dipoles in material

subtopics.name: Current
formulas: I = nqvA (Current in Terms of Drift Velocity)
definitions: Electric Current: Rate of flow of electric charge
Conventional Current: Flow direction (positive to negative)
Electron Flow: Actual direction electrons move (negative to positive)

subtopics.name: Resistance
definitions: Resistance: Opposition to flow of electric current
Resistivity: Intrinsic property of material related to resistance
Ohmic Material: Material that follows Ohm's Law

subtopics.name: Circuit Elements
definitions: Resistor: Component that impedes current flow
Capacitor: Component that stores electric charge
Inductor: Component that stores energy in magnetic field

subtopics.name: Circuit Analysis
definitions: Series Circuit: Components connected end-to-end with same current
Parallel Circuit: Components connected across same potential difference
Node: Junction point where three or more wires meet

subtopics.name: DC vs. AC
definitions: Direct Current (DC): Current flowing in one direction only
Alternating Current (AC): Current periodically changing direction
RMS Value: Effective value equivalent to DC in power delivery

subtopics.name: Magnetic Field
formulas: F = qv×B (Magnetic Force on Moving Charge)
B = μ₀I/(2πr) (Magnetic Field of Long Wire)
definitions: Magnetic Field: Region where magnetic force acts on moving charges or magnetic materials
Magnetic Flux: Measure of magnetic field passing through a surface
Magnetic Dipole: System with north and south magnetic poles

subtopics.name: Electromagnetic Induction
definitions: Electromagnetic Induction: Production of voltage by changing magnetic field
Faraday's Law: Induced EMF equals rate of change of magnetic flux
Lenz's Law: Induced current opposes the change that produced it

subtopics.name: Maxwell's Equations
definitions: Maxwell's Equations: Set of four equations describing electricity and magnetism
Electromagnetic Waves: Self-propagating waves of electric and magnetic fields

subtopics.name: EM Spectrum
definitions: Electromagnetic Spectrum: Range of all EM wave frequencies and wavelengths
Radio Waves: Lowest frequency EM waves (longest wavelength)
Microwaves: Used for communication and cooking
Infrared: Heat radiation
Visible Light: EM waves detectable by human eye (400-700 nm)
Ultraviolet: Higher energy than visible light
X-rays: High energy waves used for medical imaging
Gamma Rays: Highest frequency EM waves (shortest wavelength)

subtopics.name: Light as EM Wave
definitions: Electromagnetic Wave: Self-propagating wave of electric and magnetic fields
Light: Visible portion of electromagnetic spectrum
Wave Impedance: Ratio of electric to magnetic field in wave

subtopics.name: Polarization-Electrostatics Connection
definitions: Dipole Polarization: Alignment of molecular dipoles in electric field
Wave Polarization: Orientation of electric field oscillations in EM wave
Polarizer: Device that selectively transmits specific polarization direction

subtopics.name: Photoelectric Effect
definitions: Photocurrent: Electric current resulting from photoelectric emission
Stopping Potential: Voltage that stops photoelectrons
Quantum Efficiency: Ratio of electrons emitted to photons incident

subtopics.name: Electron-Photon Interaction
definitions: Absorption: Process where electron absorbs photon and jumps to higher energy level
Emission: Process where electron drops to lower energy level, releasing photon
Stimulated Emission: Emission triggered by incident photon (basis for lasers)
